voyage.name: Amsterdam Boats B.V.
voyage.content: Personal rental of a wide variety of boats. You can rent a gondola, hand made by a girl from Amsterdam. She traveled to Venice to learn the craft, then built her own Gondola which she brought back to Amsterdam.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Jewel Cruises
voyage.content: An evening dinner cruise. It is the only classic boat offering a private table for a romantic candlelight dinner. À la carte dining, but not cheap! The cruise starts at 19:30 and lasts just under three hours.

voyage.name: Boaty Rent a Boat
voyage.content: Boaty Rent a Boat rents small boats (max. 6 people) to make your own private boat tour on the Amsterdam canals. These rental boats are electrically driven which means they are silent and free of exhaust fumes.

voyage.name: Boats4rent Boat Rental
voyage.hours: open every day from March to October
voyage.content: Boats4rent is a boat rental where you can rent a boat without a skipper. With a three or four hour rental you can make a private trip on the Amsterdam canals and the Amstel river.

voyage.name: Boatboys Private Boat Tours
voyage.content: Operates every day for private luxury boat tours on a historic classic boat. 1hr starting from 250 EUR.

voyage.name: Canal Company
voyage.content: The Canal Hopper runs three fixed routes, stopping near major attractions (Rijksmuseum, Anne Frank's House, etc.). You can get on or off as often as you like, but it is relatively expensive with 20 EUR per 24 hours. The first boats start between 09:15 and 10:45, depending on which stop you get on. The last boats start dropping off at around 19:00. It also has four locations for renting your own boat; two-seater canal

voyage.name: Lovers Company
voyage.content: Starts opposite the Rijksmuseum, but you cannot get on or off. The cruise takes about 1 hr 30 min.

voyage.name: Sloepdelen
voyage.price: 60 EUR p/h (with a minimum of 2 hours) plus 150 EUR deposit)
voyage.content: Self operated electric rental boats. A boating license is not required and the open boats can seat up to twelve passengers.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Boat Experience
voyage.content: Amsterdam Boat Experience was founded in 2015 and has been steadily expanding its fleet and now offers exclusive private charters while also operating a fixed route from the Anne Frank house. Tickets for the 1 hour cruise on the luxurious electric open boats with live narrating are 15 EUR. while you relax the hostess serves drinks on the boat.

voyage.name: Adam's Boats
voyage.content: Rent a boat without the need for a licence. The Amstel river can be reached within 2 minutes from the hire place.

voyage.name: Starboard Boats
voyage.content: This eco friendly boat company organises luxurious private boat rentals. Starting locations on requests. From 195 EUR per hour.

voyage.name: Chinese New Year
voyage.content: Celebrated with festivities in Chinatown.

voyage.name: King's Day
voyage.content: Formerly Queen's Day, this national holiday, nominally in celebration of the King's birthday, is difficult to describe to anyone who's never been there. The city turns into one giant mass of orange-dressed people with flea markets, bands playing, and many on-street parties, ranging from small cafes placing a few kegs of beer outside to huge open-air stages hosting world-famous DJs. The Vondelpark is the place where c

voyage.name: KunstRAI
voyage.content: A modern art fair in the RAI exhibition and conference centre. If you want to know what the latest developments are in Dutch galleries, this is where to find them all in one place.

voyage.name: Holland Festival
voyage.content: A performing arts festival that brings together events from all over the world in the fields of music, opera, theater and dance.

voyage.name: Taste of Amsterdam
voyage.content: A culinary festival where you can explore the food of famous Amsterdam restaurants and their chefs.

voyage.name: Open Garden Days
voyage.content: Normally you can see only the front of the canal houses, but during the Open Garden Days you get to go past the entrance and see the green world behind them, often bigger than you would have expected. You can buy one ticket that gives you entry to all participating gardens, and there is a special canal boat to take you from one location to another.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Roots Festival
voyage.content: A free open-air festival with music from non-Western countries accompanied by paid film and theater performances in the surrounding theaters.

voyage.name: Julidans
voyage.content: International contemporary dance festival, always showing the latest developments in modern dance.

voyage.name: Vondelpark Openluchttheater
voyage.content: This free festival offers many different performances every day. Go to the open air theater just by the fountain and let the entertainment do the work. From cabaret to drama to concerts to dance, there is something for everyone here and for all ages.

voyage.name: Amsterdam International Fashion Week
voyage.content: Twice a year, this event presents young and upcoming fashion in Europe with a focus on Dutch design.

voyage.name: VriendenLoterij SummerConcerts
voyage.content: Affordable classical music concerts taking place at the prestigious Concertgebouw.

voyage.name: De Parade
voyage.content: Circus turns vintage, on an old-fashioned fairground with many different tents, the performers are each trying to attract their public, featuring spectacles of dance, theater, magic, art, animation and music.

voyage.name: Pride Amsterdam
voyage.content: Amsterdam's LGBTQIA+ pride around the first weekend in August. One of the biggest festivals in Amsterdam with parties, performances, workshops and a boat parade on the Prinsengracht on Saturday afternoon (Canal parade) which is always well worth seeing by gays and straights alike.

voyage.name: Prinsengrachtconcert and Grachtenfestival
voyage.content: Third weekend of August each year. A free open-air classical music concert is held every year on a stage in the middle of the Prinsengracht. If you have a little boat, join the crowds and make sure to bring a bottle of rose wine or prosecco for full enjoyment. It takes place during the Grachtenfestival, a 10 days classical music festival with about 150 concerts throughout the city, but is organized independently from

voyage.name: Sail Amsterdam
voyage.content: Tall-ships from all over the world come to visit the Amsterdam harbour every five years, the next one is planned in 2030.

voyage.name: National Restaurant Week
voyage.content: Two times a year, participating restaurants offer a full 3 course dinner for a mere 29.95 EUR (excluding drinks), allowing you to try a different restaurant for a change or a chance to have an affordable meal at one of the famous five-star restaurants.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Dance Event
voyage.content: Usually held during the second last weekend in October, this electronic music annual festival gathers cream of the crop faces from the house and techno scenes. Buy your tickets in advance to avoid paying more at the door and having to queue for hours. Besides partying for four nights in a row, the conference offers workshops, seminars, presentations etc.

voyage.name: Museumnacht
voyage.content: Long before the film came out, this "night at the museum" attracts new crowds at the traditional Amsterdam museums with special performances at unusual locations. Do as the locals do and hire a bike to go from one place to the other.

voyage.name: PAN Amsterdam
voyage.content: The biggest national art and antiques fair in the Netherlands.

voyage.name: International Documentary Film Festival (IDFA)
voyage.content: The largest festival in the world for documentary films with screenings of about 200 documentary films and videos.

voyage.name: Imagine Film Festival
voyage.content: A two weeks celebration of drive-in, exploitation and cult films, generally of the lower budget variety. Takes up all the screening rooms of the EYE Film Institute in Noord.

voyage.name: Museumplein
voyage.content: Amsterdam celebrates the holy day of Sint Nicholaas on 5 December as Christmas in the Dam Square also known as "Christmas Square". However, on Christmas Day, i.e. 25 December, the people of Amsterdam are also getting used to celebrating Christmas alongside English speakers.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Light Festival
voyage.content: Outdoor light installations/artworks exposition in the canals of Binnenstad. Each year the festival has a different theme.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Centraal railway station
voyage.content: This beautiful building is an attraction in itself, so if you did not arrive in Amsterdam by train, it is well worth making a special trip to look at the station's facade. The station was built between 1881 and 1889 on three artificial islands. It was designed by Pierre Cuypers who also designed the Rijksmuseum in a similar neo-late-Gothic/Renaissance style. At the time, the project was highly controversial as the ne

voyage.name: Beurs van Berlage
voyage.content: Take a guided tour and check out the view from the top of the old stock exchange tower. It was built in 1903 (by Hendrik Petrus Berlage) and is considered the beginning of modern Dutch architecture. Costs €3.50, located on Beursplein near Dam Square.

voyage.name: Royal Palace
voyage.content: The Royal Palace is one of the three official palaces of the Netherlands. It is at the disposal of King Willem-Alexander by the Act of Parliament. It was built in 1651 as the city hall of Amsterdam, in a period known as the Dutch Golden Age. Many school children learn that because of the swampy soil, it was built on no less than 13,569 wooden poles. In 1795, the French Empire of Napoleon Bonaparte invaded the Netherl

voyage.name: Nationaal Monument
voyage.content: A large spire that functions as a memorial for the victims of World War II. It was designed by architect J.J.P. Oud and revealed on 4 May 1956. Every 4 May, at the Remembrance of the Dead, a ceremony is held here to commemorate all civilians and members of the Dutch armed forces that died in World War II and later armed conflicts.

voyage.name: Begijnhof
voyage.content: The Begijnhof is a late medieval enclosed courtyard with the houses of beguines (Roman Catholic women living in a semi-religious community). It is a very picturesque group of historic buildings, mostly private dwellings. House number 34 is the oldest home in Amsterdam. The courtyard also has a Reformed Church and a hidden Catholic chapel. Surprisingly, it feels like a serene oasis as it is surrounded by the chaotic K

voyage.name: Esnoga
voyage.content: The most prominent synagogue of the city centre, the Esnoga dates back from 1675 and is built in an austere Classicist style. In 1492, Spain expelled its Jewish population as part of the Inquisition, and many fled to Portugal. One hundred years later, their descendants migrated to Amsterdam for its religious freedom. This happened at a time when the Dutch provinces were fighting for independence against Spain. As to

voyage.name: Nieuwe Kerk
voyage.price: By credit/debit card only: adult €19.50, student/youth €9.50, child under 12 free, free with Museumkaart
voyage.content: Used for royal coronations, including the crowning of King Willem-Alexander in 2013, and royal weddings, including his wedding to princess Máxima in 2002. The church is no longer used for services but is now a popular exhibition space. Admissions are limited: by tickets online to reserve a space.

voyage.name: Oude Kerk
voyage.content: The oldest of the five main churches in the historic centre, and probably the oldest building in Amsterdam. It is right in the heart of the Red Light District. You can climb the tower from April to September on Saturday and Sunday, every half-hour. Also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) cost €70 per hour. E-mail for more information.

voyage.name: Zuiderkerk
voyage.content: Built in 1603-1611. Located on Zuiderkerkhof ("Southern Graveyard"). Now an information centre on housing and planning. You can visit the tower from April to September Monday to Saturday (with guide only) every half-hour, cost €6. Also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 15 people) cost €70 per hr. E-mail for more information.

voyage.name: Allard Pierson Museum
voyage.content: The Allard Pierson Museum is the archaeological museum of the University of Amsterdam. The ancient civilizations of Egypt, Cyprus, the Greek world, Etruria and the Roman Empire are revived in this museum. Art objects and utensils, dating from 4000 B.C. till 500 A.D. give a good impression of everyday life, mythology and religion in Antiquity.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Museum
voyage.content: A museum about the history of Amsterdam.

voyage.name: Civic Guards Gallery
voyage.content: Just inside the arched gateway to the Amsterdam Museum is a hidden passageway with fifteen enormous 17th-century paintings; entrance is free to the public during museum hours. The collection features massive and meticulously realistic portraits of wealthy citizens from the Dutch Golden Age, the same class of subjects Rembrandt depicted in the most famous of Civic Guard paintings, the "Night Watch".

voyage.name: Jewish Historical Museum
voyage.content: Jewish Historical Museum. History of the Jewish people, culture and religion.

voyage.name: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
voyage.content: One of the oldest museums in Amsterdam, this is a Catholic church stuffed into the upper stories of a house built in 1663, when Catholics were persecuted and had to disguise their churches. It's amazing to see how they fit worshippers, an organ, and an altar into such a narrow place.

voyage.name: Oranje Voetbal Museum
voyage.content: The legacy of Dutch football started in the 1970s, when Total Football, a revolutionary Dutch style of football, shook the world. The Netherlands is the best football nation that never won the World Cup: it lost the final three times, a national trauma. It did win the European Cup in 1988 lead by star player Marco van Basten. This museum has four floors dedicated to "Oranje", and a small cinema that shows a 20-minute

voyage.name: Rembrandt House
voyage.content: This is where the artist Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn and his wife, Saskia, lived between 1639 and 1658. The house is a reconstruction of the painter’s life at that time and provides interesting insight. You will be able to see 260 of his 290 etchings, find out about how they were created, see where he worked and explore the nooks and crannies of this fascinating building.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Music Theatre
voyage.content: Opera, dance, ballet and other performances. Holds a free lunch concert on Tuesdays.

voyage.name: NEMO
voyage.content: Above a tunnel overseeing the IJ, NEMO is the largest science museum in the Netherlands. It's a showcase of how scientific phenomena influence daily life. Different sections of the museum deal with technology and engineering, ICT, and bio- and behavioral sciences. This is a place to take kids and is best for those ages 11 and below—teenagers will probably get bored. And it is usually definitely full of children on we

voyage.name: Gassan Diamonds
voyage.content: A guided tour is given that's all about the diamond production process and the history of diamond trade in Amsterdam. Diamonds have been traded in Amsterdam for longer than 425 years, and the city used to be known as the "City of Diamonds". Tours are given in 27 languages. Of course you can also buy Gassan diamonds here, but you don't have to.

voyage.name: Hash, Marihuana and Hemp Museum
voyage.content: Opened for over twenty years, the Hash Museum is dedicated to debunking the lies and demonization about one of our most useful plants, the hemp plant. Although small, busy and seriously overpriced, it is a well-done museum where people go to get informed.

voyage.name: Sexmuseum
voyage.content: The largest and most prestigious museum for sex art and sex history in the Netherlands. It shows a lot of sex oddities. Only ages 16 and up are allowed entry.

voyage.name: Madame Tussauds
voyage.content: The well-known franchise of wax museums also has a branch in Amsterdam. It's a major tourist attraction so expect a steep entry fee and long queues. Unique to this branch are waxworks of famous Dutch people including Willem-Alexander, Beatrix, Tiësto, Rafael van der Vaart, Doutzen Kroes, Vincent van Gogh and Rembrandt.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Dungeon
voyage.content: The Amsterdam Dungeon is a horror tour through several dark chambers with live actors.

voyage.name: Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments
voyage.content: The latest gimmicky tourist attraction near the Centraal Station, it's a small museum about medieval torture and torture devices. In the Middle Ages, torture was a widely known punishment for almost all crimes committed, ranging from rape to murder, and above all for heresy. The type of punishment depended on the victim's crime and social status. The Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments displays over 100 devices us

voyage.name: Torture Museum
voyage.content: You'd think one museum about torture would be enough, but no, not in Amsterdam. However, this was the first torture museum in the city centre, and is at least somewhat more authentic than the copycat. The museum depicts the history of different torturous techniques used over the centuries. The lighting is bad, the corridors are small and the price an absolute rip-off. You can walk through it in 15-30 minutes.

voyage.name: Spui
voyage.content: Every Friday and Sunday a market is held on the Spui. Friday has books on sale, while Sundays are all about art and antiques.

voyage.name: Waterloopleinmarkt
voyage.content: A well-known but fairly overrated market near the city hall. Partly flea market, partly alternative and second hand clothing and accessories. More oriented towards tourists than to locals.

voyage.name: The American Book Center
voyage.content: Excellent shop for literature and books in the English language, particularly on American culture.

voyage.name: Athenaeum Boekhandel
voyage.content: One of the most renowned bookstores of Amsterdam because of its wide array of fiction and more academic titles. It is very popular among local students; however, their study books are also interesting reading material for non-graduates. They have a particular large selection of books in the humanities, including history, media, language, culture and international relations. Also has a Newscentre with a wide variety o

voyage.name: The Book Exchange
voyage.content: A second-hand bookstore specialising in English books, and has a large selection, with an especially good selection of travel writing, detectives, and SF/fantasy.

voyage.name: Waterstones
voyage.content: Another good tip for English literature. Prices on the high side, but there's a good selection of fiction and children's books. They also have magazines, newspapers and board games.

voyage.name: Scheltema
voyage.content: One of the largest bookstores in the Netherlands, with a wide selection on five clearly arranged floors with over 125,000 titles for study, travel, cooking, art, history, philosophy, culture and literature.

voyage.name: De Bijenkorf
voyage.content: High-end department store, one of the flagship stores of this chain which opened in 1870. This building on Dam square opened in 1915 and has been a national heritage site since 2021. After a series of expansions throughout the 20th century, the store covers 20,000 m² of retail space.

voyage.name: HEMA Nieuwendijk
voyage.content: Midrange department/variety chain store, with 540 branches in the Netherlands. This store is one of the flagship stores of this chain which opened in 1926. Besides daily basics, you can also find original Dutch designs. Besides local food products specific linked to this store like the pastry "tompouce" and a sausage "rookworst", you can also find products with Miffy (Nijntje), Takkie and Siepie. The latter two are a

voyage.name: Gebr. Niemeijer
voyage.content: French-style bakery with pastries, croissants, breads, sandwiches all baked fresh on premises. Open for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeaway. Bring the kids and eat in the small playroom upstairs.

voyage.name: Van der Linde
voyage.content: Its officially a bakery, but they don't sell bread. They do sell Amsterdam's most famous whipped ice cream, lovely almond cookies and cakes. The texture is really creamy and soft, it melts easily and they put it in a cone with a soup spoon.

voyage.name: Haring & Zo
voyage.content: Serving for example fish sandwiches

voyage.name: Rob Wigboldus Fishmonger
voyage.content: Herring sandwiches for €3.50.

voyage.name: Pasta Pasta
voyage.content: Serves delicious pastas, made just as you want them. Choose a sauce, topping and pasta for a tasty, but well-priced meal.

voyage.name: Julia's
voyage.content: Italian cuisine, both eat-in and take-out; notable take-out item: Penne Bolognese with a tasty vegetarian sauce instead of a meat sauce.

voyage.name: OCHA
voyage.content: This used to be just the little "Thai snackbar around the corner", but since a raving review in the local newspaper Het Parool, big crowds are waiting in line to get seated during dinnertime. The scenery is simple and the restaurant is very small and cramped. However, the hype is all about the food, which is absolutely mouth-watering. They have the usual Thai fare, but the dish to go for is the massaman curry, their

voyage.name: Thaise Snackbar Bird
voyage.content: Very crowded little snack bar with Thai food. Not to be confused with the restaurant of the same owner, on the other side of the street. Try the chicken in oyster sauce.

voyage.name: New King
voyage.content: Slowly becoming an institution, this hugely popular Mandarin Chinese restaurant seems to have found a perfect balance between food, price and ambiance. The food is authentically Chinese, delicious, fresh and quickly served, and all of that for a bargain. Service is fast and rushed, but it doesn't feel like a snack bar. It has a stylish interior, and it's still one of those places you could bring a date to. The bigges

voyage.name: Greetje
voyage.content: Traditional Dutch, alongside French classics. Located in an historic building on a quiet side street near Central Station; it's off the beaten track so most of the diners are local. Open 6 days a week (not Mondays); a reservation is usually necessary.

voyage.name: Kantjil & de Tijger
voyage.content: Great spices and meat dishes, Indian/Indonesian food. Try the Nasi Goreng Rames.

voyage.name: Rembrandt Corner
voyage.content: Around the corner of the "Rembrandt Huis" is a very nice "Eetcafe" with fresh food, WiFi hot spots and internet workplaces. Try the dish of the day or the mussels.

voyage.name: Tony's NY City Bagels
voyage.content: Oversized cups of coffee, muffins and bagels. Muffins, brownies, giant cookies, cheesecake and bagels spread with various toppings are served at reasonable prices to a clientèle that is a mix of locals and tourists. American themed. There are 3 locations in the city.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Jewel Cruises
voyage.content: À la carte dining while cruising the canals.

voyage.name: Blue
voyage.content: The selling point of this cafe is its 360 degrees view over Amsterdam. Its interior is minimalist and stylish. A great place to have a Dutch cup of coffee while taking in the views. Unfortunately, it's only open at daytime as evenings are reserved for private events.

voyage.name: De Jaren
voyage.content: A minimal art-deco interior next to Hotel d'Europe and a great view of where all the main canals come together (climb the stairs to the upper floor - the view is better and the crowds surprisingly thinner). Food is middling and on the pricy side, but it's a nice place to sip a cup of coffee or tea and read a newspaper.

voyage.name: Filter
voyage.content: Small eco-friendly coffeebar situated in the lobby of hotel Ecomama. Serves great coffee, breakfast and a small selection of sweet and savoury treats. Also organic tea, juice and the best grilled-cheese sandwiches. Have a relaxed morning on the sunny terrace or enjoy art by starting Dutch artists.

voyage.name: The Grasshopper
voyage.content: On the edge of the Red Light District, has an upper-floor bar.

voyage.name: Hannekes Boom
voyage.content: One of Amsterdam's hidden secrets, Hannekes Boom is a cosy, somewhat ramshackle, bar with a waterfront along the IJ. It's a great place to just hang out and have a beer. Not for clubbers, but for those looking for a relaxing underground atmosphere and live music. It is centrally located, but off the tourist path, so it has a local feel to it. Outdoor seating is available, but you have to order your drinks inside. If

voyage.name: Brouwerij de Prael
voyage.price: Brewery tour 7.50 EUR or 16.50 EUR, beer tasting with four beers €10
voyage.hours: Beer shop 12:00-19:00, tasting room Tue-Sat 12:00-24:00, Sun 12:00-23:00
voyage.content: A brewery, tasting room and beer shop all in one.

voyage.name: Cracked Kettle
voyage.content: This beer, wine, and spirits shop carries independent, unique, and rare bottles. The staff are friendly, but the space is quite confined and obtaining bottles from the very top shelves requires assistance and a dust rag.

voyage.name: De Bierkoning
voyage.content: Not a café, but a 'supermarket' specialized in beer. It has over a thousand beers, about half of it Dutch.

voyage.name: In De Wildeman
voyage.content: A very well stocked beer café, or actually beer tasting room (bierproeflokaal) in the centre of the inner city. 17 beers (usually from various countries) and a cider on draught, and about 250 different bottled beers offered. There is no music played, which makes for a very friendly and talkative atmosphere, and it has a separate non-smoking room.

voyage.name: Wynand Fockink
voyage.content: Wynand Fockink is a distillery that started in 1679. They offer distillery tours, but you must reserve at least a week in advance as they fill up quickly. It is also a tasting room and a liquor store. They have numerous liquors, brandies, and jenevers and encourage you to try them all. It is traditional to stoop and sip the first drink and not spill. Great liquors, and a good time in the back alleys of Amsterdam.

voyage.name: Belgique
voyage.content: One of the smallest bars in Amsterdam, there is seating for at most 15 people. Specialising in Belgian beers, extensive menu that includes some hard to find beers on tap. This place is smoke friendly so don't be surprised to see people rolling joints as they drink.

voyage.name: Cuba
voyage.content: Great bar, really nice atmosphere, close to the Red Light District with a nice terrace in the summer. Selection of cheap cocktails and long island ice tea.

voyage.name: Gollem
voyage.content: A special beer café, serving many beers, especially from Belgium, Germany, Czech Republic and other countries.

voyage.name: Katoen
voyage.content: Close to the southern part of the Canal District. Alternative music and cosy atmosphere also in the evenings.

voyage.name: Molly Malones Irish Pub
voyage.content: Authentic Irish pub with food. Mix of expatriates, locals and tourists, friendly staff, on a canal off the Zeedijk, close to Centraal Station and Warmoesstraat. Open every night, live music in the week-ends and large-screen television.

voyage.name: Schuim
voyage.content: The super comfy cafe is a great place to spend entire rainy days at a time. It heats up quite a bit at night. Pot smoking seems to be tolerated even though Schuim is definitely not a "coffeeshop".

voyage.name: Speijk
voyage.content: Awesome bar with lost of fun, artsy crazy locals. Various DJ play different styles. Open till late in the morning. Best place to meet laid-back and awesome Amsterdammers!!

voyage.name: Irish Pub Slainte
voyage.content: An Irish pub that also serves very inexpensive food like cheese sandwiches. Everything you can expect from an Irish pub nearby the Oude Kerk and nearby the Red Light District.

voyage.name: Bitterzoet
voyage.content: This placed used to be alternative, but changed ownership and is now more hip hop and R&B oriented. Check their agenda to see what they're doing.

voyage.name: Winston Kingdom
voyage.content: Music venue and nightclub in the red light district.

voyage.name: 420CAFE
voyage.content: Known for their moderate prices. The music played here is Classic Rock & Frank Zappa.

voyage.name: Bluebird
voyage.content: One of the best selections of pot in Amsterdam.

voyage.name: De Dampkring
voyage.content: The shop was featured in a scene in Ocean's Twelve. Very decent hashish ("Rifman" products), rather high prices. Has won the Cannabis Cup numerous times.

voyage.name: Green House
voyage.content: Usually pretty crowded but when warm or if you can get a seat definitely one of the nice coffeeshops near the Red Light District. Also has a bar next door.

voyage.name: Hill Street Blues
voyage.content: Lively atmosphere but buy cannabis elsewhere.

voyage.name: Kadinsky
voyage.content: It looks completely different from before, and now has three floors with a slick minimalist design.A great place to smoke your goods, and actually serves a good cup of coffee too.

voyage.name: Bulldog
voyage.price: Breakfast, sheets, shower and a locker starting at €22
voyage.content: Friendly hostel in the heart of the Red Light District. A coffeeshop is conveniently located on the ground floor, this is also where you get your breakfast.

voyage.name: Durty Nellys Inn
voyage.content: Dorms are clean and the beds comfortable. The Irish pub downstairs gives discounts to people staying in the hostel (€3.5 for a pint of Amstel, €6 for a burger and chips). Breakfast 09:00-11:00. No common area apart from the bar itself.

voyage.name: Flying Pig Downtown
voyage.content: The "Downtown" branch, as opposed to the "Uptown" in Zuid, has more of a party vibe. Both hostels are known for their laid-back atmosphere, bars and indoor smoking areas. Free extras, check out the facility page on their website.

voyage.name: Hotel Beursstraat
voyage.content: Simple and clean hotel, mostly visited by (young) people who are looking for an inexpensive accommodation.

voyage.name: Hotel Brian
voyage.content: Very basic hotel, but breakfast and internet included.

voyage.name: Hotel Tamara
voyage.content: Cheap "hotel" in a great location with basic clean rooms.

voyage.name: Intersail Hostel Avontuur
voyage.price: 4-bed private from €22.50-27.50 per bed per night. 2- and 3-bed private from 25-30 EUR per bed per night
voyage.content: A floating hostel. Small cabins, bed-length is 1.90 m, but great staff and a nice spacious sun deck. Breakfast, sheets, towels are included in the price. Shared shower and toilet. Four person cabins are better to be used for only three adults. Don't take too much luggage in these cabins.

voyage.name: Shelter City Christian Hostel
voyage.content: An alcohol and drug-free Christian youth hostel right at the Red Light District. Single-sex dormitories, including breakfast, bed linen.

voyage.name: St Christophers
voyage.content: Part hostel, part hotel. Each room is designed by local Dutch artists.

voyage.name: Stayokay Stadsdoelen
voyage.content: Stayokay operates a network of 27 hostels in the Netherlands, and is the Dutch affiliate of Hostelling International. A little smaller than Stayokay Vondelpark, this location does not take groups. Free WiFi and pay internet terminals. Free security lockers are provided in the hallways outside the dorms. One of the few hostels in town who can accept under 18 year olds traveling alone (granted you have a written permis

voyage.name: Travel Hotel Amsterdam
voyage.content: The hotel is a comfortable 2-star hotel a 5-minute walk from Amsterdam’s Central Station.

voyage.name: White Tulip Hostel
voyage.content: Mostly dorms, but there are also a few private rooms available. Really a basic crash-pad, but quiet and relaxed due to their 'No large groups' policy.

voyage.name: Hostel Meeting Point
voyage.content: Laid-back hostel. Has his own, pretty cheap, hotel bar. Smoking room (weed allowed) inside. Guests of the hostel can use free internet computers. Only dorms.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Bed and Breakfast Canal View
voyage.content: Has nice canal view rooms.

voyage.name: Delta Hotel
voyage.content: Clean rooms and friendly staff.

voyage.name: Hotel Continental
voyage.content: Small rooms. Shared toilets.

voyage.name: Rembrandtplein Hotel
voyage.content: Friendly staff, bar open all night.

voyage.name: RHo Hotel
voyage.content: Rooms are quiet. Parking available. Friendly staff.

voyage.name: Rokin Hotel
voyage.content: A 2-star renovated 17th century mansion. Very clean and good atmosphere, own parking.

voyage.name: Jewel Canal Apartments
voyage.content: Two canalside apartments in the center of Amsterdam, close to the Dam Square. Suitable for holiday and business stays. Free high speed internet.

voyage.name: Estheréa
voyage.content: A boutique hotel that consists of a row of 17th-century buildings along the Singel canal. It has 93 rooms and 2 suites. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Amrâth Amsterdam
voyage.content: An upscale hotel established in the monumental Scheepvaarthuis, the first building in Amsterdam School style that used to be the headquarters of six shipping companies. Breakfast is not included in the lower rates, but all include Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Anantara Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky
voyage.content: A somewhat seedy location for a 5-star hotel, the main entrance is right on Dam Square, but the hotel backs onto the red-light district, with a view of sex-shops and peepshows.

voyage.name: Park Plaza Victoria Amsterdam
voyage.content: A 4-star immediately opposite Centraal Station. Free Wi-Fi in public spaces.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel, Amsterdam City Center
Renaissance Amsterdam
voyage.content: A 4-star hotel with conference centre, Wi-Fi access in the lobby and café.

voyage.name: Sofitel Legend The Grand
voyage.content: The Sofitel has views on the canals. Weather permitting, lunch is served in the courtyard.

voyage.name: Magere Brug
voyage.content: The Magere Brug, literally "Skinny Bridge", is a bridge that spans the Amstel River and connects the Kerkstraat with the Nieuwe Kerkstraat. It's an iconic bridge that consists of nine arches and a drawbridge that is still operated by hand. The current bridge is made of white-painted wood, but it has been rebuilt several times and historically it has also been in concrete. The first bridge here was built in 1691, but

voyage.name: Anne Frank House
voyage.hours: 9:00 - 22:00 (shorter on some national holidays, closed 25 September)
voyage.content: The house where the Jewish girl Anne Frank wrote her diary while hiding with her family from the Nazis. One must buy tickets online, only 20% are issued on the same day so buy them in advance. During high season tickets can be sold out a month in advance. To be safe, you should book 6 weeks in advance. Museumkaart is valid, I Amsterdam Card is not valid.

voyage.name: Museum Het Grachtenhuis
voyage.content: Het Grachtenhuis is the gateway to the world-famous Canal District. Het Grachtenhuis tells the fascinating story of how Amsterdam's Canal District was created by a multi-media exhibition.

voyage.name: Cat Cabinet
voyage.content: A cat museum. Housed in a beautiful restored palatial home in an upscale area street - very Masterpiece Theater. It was opened by the homeowner after his favourite cat died... and he still lives in the home. Lots of cat-related art, and two real felines. The exhibition is spread across the first floor of the house.

voyage.name: Museum Willet-Holthuysen
voyage.content: It is the only fully furnished canalside patrician house in Amsterdam that is open to the public. The museum has a large collection of silverware, plates, and books from the Dutch Golden Age. It also has a substantial collection of art.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Pipe Museum
voyage.content: Unique collection of smoking pipes in an authentic canal house from 1670. In the historic ambience of the collector's house, his collection of pipes covering 2,500 years is displayed. Visitors get a personal tour by enthusiast volunteers of the foundation that also runs the speciality shop in the basement: a huge selection of nearly 3,000 modern briar pipes are for sale, next to collectables and books on pipes and to

voyage.name: Museum Van Loon
voyage.content: 17th century house with interior restored with furnishings to how it looked in the 18th century. Also interesting to see a garden you would not normally see from the streets.

voyage.name: Foam
voyage.content: Museum about photography. Group tours can be arranged via phone at +31 20 5516 505.

voyage.name: Westerkerk
voyage.content: Built in 1620-1631, located on Westermarkt near the Anne Frank House. You can climb the tower (with a guide only) every half hour, M-Sa €6. The tower is also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) for €70/hr. In good weather you can see all of Amsterdam, and as far as the coast. Free organ concert held every Friday at 13:00.

voyage.name: Homomonument
voyage.content: The Homomonument is a memorial to gays and lesbians murdered in World War II, a call for vigilance against homophobia, and an inspiration for gays and lesbians the world over. It consists of three equilateral triangles made of pink granite that are connected by an inlaid band of pink bricks. These three triangles represent the past, present and future.

voyage.name: Rembrandtplein
voyage.content: This public square features a larger-than-life statue of Rembrandt on a pedestal.

voyage.name: De Poezenboot
voyage.content: You really like cats? The poezenboot (cat boat) is a refuge for cats awaiting adoption.

voyage.name: Ignatiushuis
voyage.content: A Jesuit society that organizes classes and activities. Membership is required, but every Tuesday (Sep-Jul) a free concert is given at 12:30-13:00. Everyone can attend.

voyage.name: Pathé Tuschinski
voyage.content: Since its opening in 1921, Tuschinski has been the country's most breathtaking film theatre. It's worth a visit if only for its interior, a spectacular mix of Art Nouveau, Amsterdam School and Art Deco styles. If possible, get a tour of the building, taking in the sumptuous private rooms upstairs. If you're going to watch a film, pick the one that's in the big auditorium. With the exception of some animated films, al

voyage.name: Stadsarchief Amsterdam
voyage.content: This institute maintains the archives of the municipality and other organizations that are closely related to Amsterdam. The archives are open to everyone. Most interesting for travelers are the exhibitions and events, see the website.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Booze Cruise
voyage.content: A boat trip through the canals of Amsterdam is always a good idea. Discover Amsterdam from the water while enjoying a drink.

voyage.name: Bloemenmarkt
voyage.content: The world's only floating flower market, open daily on the Singel between Koningsplein and Muntplein. It is very touristy, but you could do worse than buying your tulips here. Make sure you buy pre-approved bulbs if taking them to the U.S. or Canada. They will have the holographic licence and export tag on the bag.

voyage.name: The Nine Streets
voyage.content: Nine narrow streets enclosed between the main canals from the Prinsengracht to the Singel, southwest of Dam Square. The northernmost street is Reestraat and to the south is the Runstraat. The street names are marked with a sign of the Nine Streets, and some shops have a flyer of this area. You can find a lot of boutiques, specialist shops, galleries and restaurants here.

voyage.name: De Beeldenwinkel Sculpture Gallery
voyage.content: This is a gallery for sculpture lovers, with bronze statues, pottery, abstract sculpture, raku-fired statues and marble figures sculpture to suit every budget and taste.

voyage.name: Pancakes! Amsterdam
voyage.content: Amazing variety of both sweet and savory pancakes. The quaint atmosphere and the street side tables are great for watching people. The only downfall is that street-side tables attract too many tourists asking for directions.

voyage.name: The Pancake Bakery
voyage.content: Large selection of sweet or savory pancakes.

voyage.name: Frens Haringhandel
voyage.content: A stall offering simple Dutch seafood fare like Kibbling (fried fish) and Haring (raw herring).

voyage.name: De Blauwe Hollander
voyage.content: Dutch restaurant with an extensive menu of hearty home-cooked dishes like herrings, pea soup and hutspot. Unlike most restaurants in this area, this one gets local diners too, and if it gets crowded enough you may have to share tables. Pancakes are served only until 17:00.

voyage.name: Damsteeg
voyage.content: They specialise in fish dishes, but they also have a wide variety of meat and vegetarian meals to choose from. With bar.

voyage.name: Letting
voyage.content: Indian-owned breakfast, brunch and lunch spot. Letting offers a range of soups, sandwiches and scones, and it's on a street which is packed with an ever-changing line-up of fun boutiques.

voyage.name: Holtkamp
voyage.content: Best pastry cafe in Amsterdam. Much better than the Zeitan, which many recommend. Do try the "holdkampf" with fillings! The Sachertorte is famous as a favorite of the former Queen Beatrix.

voyage.name: Alberto's Steakhouse
voyage.content: Uruguayan Steakhouse with well-grilled steaks

voyage.name: Akbar
voyage.content: Indian restaurant, Muslim (halal) / Hindu (no beef). Good quality dishes from different regions of India.

voyage.name: La Margarita
voyage.content: This Caribbean restaurant offers a huge range of plates, including three different vegetarian options. Every dish comes with ample sides of white rice, black beans, plantains, and vegetables. In addition to having great food, the restaurant is decked out with a range of fantastic and magic-realist art. If you like your food hot, then be sure to ask for the special homemade hot sauce. Reservations accepted.

voyage.name: 't Arendsnest
voyage.content: Excellent biercafe serving only Dutch beers and liqueurs, including jenever. Around 30 beers on tap, 17 or so which change regularly, and over 100 bottled. Very friendly bartenders who know beer well and give great recommendations. Try the €8 sampler, which gives you 12cl (1.2ml) samples of 3 beers with a glass of water and some crackers.

voyage.name: Dan Murphy's
voyage.content: One of the many Irish pubs in the city. People from all over the world meet here and watch football, rugby and typical Irish sports like hurling and Gaelic football while drinking a pint of Guinness.

voyage.name: Feijoa
voyage.content: Cocktail bar with a lovely atmosphere, pleasant music and friendly staff, including one of the Netherlands leading cocktail barmen. Will make any cocktail you ask for.

voyage.name: Hard Rock Cafe
voyage.content: This is close to, or right next to the Holland Casino also close to the Leidseplein. Great service, great food, and plenty of drinks.

voyage.name: Mulligans Irish Music Bar
voyage.content: The oldest Irish bar in Amsterdam, Mulligans has live music most nights. This is where the traditional music crowd gathers.

voyage.name: l'Opera
voyage.content: A friendly spot for coffee, a beer, or something stronger. You may at first only notice the outside seating and the enclosed terrace, but there is also an elegant, (usually) quieter indoor area. Food, too, but you don't see many eaters.

voyage.name: Whisky Cafe L&B
voyage.content: If you like whisky, this small, laid-back and friendly cafe is the ideal place to visit. Many unusual whiskies from independent bottlers and closed distilleries are available. The menu stretches along one wall and is about 2 meters in height, the cafe having had 1001 whiskies available since it opened. Just be warned the stairs to the toilets are pretty steep!

voyage.name: Chicago Social Club
voyage.content: Amsterdam's nightlife king Casper Reinders joined with the founders of Bitterzoet and the owners of Boom Chicago to bring quality clubbing to the Leidspelein.

voyage.name: Escape
voyage.content: A large, fairly uninspiring nightclub that mostly plays mainstream house music. The first hall is large and attracts the more or less wannabe hip people of the city, although the crowd is diverse. The second hall upstairs has a completely different audience, mostly hip-hop and R&B enthusiasts. At some events, Escape is split in two, which means you can use the backside entry at Amstel for a different party.

voyage.name: Jimmy Woo
voyage.content: The most glamorous club in Amsterdam offers a selection of house and R&B, with a spectacularly lit dance floor downstairs. It is relatively small and there is table service, so it feels a bit like a VIP room. Entry policy is strict so dress sharp to get in. And boys, don't come alone.

voyage.name: Melkweg
voyage.content: A former milk factory, now it's one of the best live venues in Amsterdam. Its interior is not as good as Paradiso, but it feels more like a nightclub as the music is dance/trance-oriented. Popular among university students and younger tourists, it's a great place to go out till the sun gets up. Rates can vary widely, and go very steep during special events.

voyage.name: Paradiso
voyage.content: Sometimes referred to as a nightclub, it feels more like a nightly music venue and is the safest bet in town. Its interior is phenomenal as it is housed in a former church, but the main room has relatively bad acoustics. It gets a mixed crowd as there are plenty of rooms with different bands performing and it isn't too crazy expensive. Its music straddles the line between pop and alternative. Much of the performances

voyage.name: Studio 80
voyage.content: This is a somewhat more underground, intimate club that's easy to miss because of its flashy neighbours. It prides itself on trying to stay at the forefront of electronic music in the city.

voyage.name: Sugar Factory
voyage.content: Bit of a remarkable place that integrates art, music, culture, theatre and nightclub into one. It has a relaxed atmosphere with an eccentric, artistic audience.

voyage.name: The Cave Rockclub
voyage.content: Cozy metal bar with friendly bar staff and interesting regulars, with live performances by touring metal bands on weekends.

voyage.name: Waterhole
voyage.content: Light rock/funk jam sessions in a dingy but atmospheric bar with pooltables. Live bands play every night of the week.

voyage.name: Betty Too
voyage.content: Absolute gem, cozy and friendly place with moderate prizes and interesting, international crowd.

voyage.name: Bulldog
voyage.content: This is the original shop that used to be a police department. Now it turned into a chain of touristy coffeeshops, bars, hotels and even an energy drink.

voyage.name: Global Chillage
voyage.content: Good produce and nice tunes but uncomfortable seating.

voyage.name: Grey Area
voyage.content: Tiny, but famous for their outstanding weed, especially "American" strains.

voyage.name: The Otherside
voyage.content: Gay coffeeshop.

voyage.name: Hans Brinker Hostel
voyage.content: Very light atmosphere and doesn't take itself seriously. Bar and downstairs club.

voyage.name: Mozart Hotel
voyage.content: 47 en-suite rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Asterisk
voyage.price: €70, knock off a couple of euros by booking directly on their site
voyage.content: Smallish, but clean and quiet rooms in two buildings across a residential street. Generous check-in/checkout, good breakfast (included). Close to tram stop, walk to Rijks/van Gogh museums.

voyage.name: Blue Moon Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: Bed & Breakfast opposite the Rijksmuseum.

voyage.name: Cocomama
voyage.content: Amsterdam's first boutique hostel. Free wifi, garden, fully equipped kitchen for guest use, livingroom. Very social atmosphere. All rooms en suite.

voyage.name: Hotel La Boheme
voyage.content: Two star hotel with very friendly staff. Clean rooms and free wi fi.

voyage.name: Hotel Nicolaas Witsen
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in the city center of Amsterdam nearby Heineken factory.

voyage.name: Clayton Hotel Amsterdam American
voyage.content: Listed as an Art Nouveau monument, the hotel is right in the heart of Leidseplein Square. Both Café Americain and Bar Americain are in the hotel, famous for celebrity and VIP spotting.

voyage.name: Hotel Ambassade
voyage.content: Four star hotel on one of the main canals. Writers who stayed here left signed copies of their books in the hotel's library.

voyage.name: Hotel Pulitzer
voyage.content: 25 restored 17th and 18th-century canal houses overlooking two of the city's most picturesque canals, Prinsengracht and Keizersgracht, and made famous in Ocean's 12.

voyage.name: Natura Artis Magistra Zoo
voyage.price: Youth (3 to 9 years) €18, adult (10 to 64 years) €21.50, seniors (65 +) €17.50
voyage.content: An entry ticket for Artis also provides admission to the Planetarium, the Aquarium and the Zoological Museum. Artis is also a botanical garden, with plants and trees gathered from all over the world, just like the animal species. Don't miss the Artis ZOOmeravonden.

voyage.name: Hortus Botanicus
voyage.content: The Amsterdam Botanical Gardens — 'Hortus' as they are called by locals — used to be the Botanic Garden of the University of Amsterdam. It is one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world. Nowadays it is an independent organisation. The collection of the garden consists of more than 6,000 species. The garden regularly holds extra exhibitions and music performances.

voyage.name: Wertheimpark
voyage.content: A small park with a World War II memorial located at one of the nicest canals in Amsterdam.

voyage.name: H'ART
voyage.price: Standard (adults and children aged 18 or over) €22.50, children up to 17 years old free
voyage.content: Founded as an outpost of the Hermitage in St Petersburg, ties were severed with the parent institution following Russia's war in Ukraine. After a hasty rebrand, the H'ART museum reopened in April 2022 with a focus on Dutch heritage in Amsterdam.

voyage.name: Scheepvaartmuseum
voyage.content: Het Scheepvaartmuseum reopened in late 2011 following major renovations. Stimulating, interactive exhibitions allow visitors to explore 500 years of maritime history. The building, called the Arsenal, is impressive. The Central Square, the indoor courtyard can be visited for free and takes your breath away. Also the museum shop, the restaurant and the library are open to the public free of charge.

voyage.name: Verzetsmuseum
voyage.content: Museum showing what Amsterdam and Holland were like during Nazi occupation. Has a very nice children's section. If you are visiting with kids and want to go to a museum about the Second World War in the Netherlands this is definitely recommended.

voyage.name: De Gooyer
voyage.content: It's the only windmill (1814, restored) in the centre of Amsterdam, and the closest one that's open to visitors.

voyage.name: Micropia
voyage.content: Museum about microbes.

voyage.name: Carré Theatre
voyage.content: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was meant as a permanent circus building. It is mainly used for musicals, cabaret performances and pop concerts.

voyage.name: Kriterion
voyage.content: Nice small movie theatre. Also has a bar.

voyage.name: Cafe Kadijk
voyage.content: Cafe Kadijk is a small Indonesian restaurant that offers good food at a decent price. The restaurant has a coffee shop vibe and is located in a "trendy" area. Just outside Amsterdam's city centre, it is a bit of a walk away from the more touristy areas of the city. Patio dining and indoor dining are both available.

voyage.name: De plantage
voyage.content: Big restaurant with a nice terrace in the summer, open all day with breakfast, lunch and dinner.

voyage.name: Restaurant Plancius
voyage.content: Has a nice high tea.

voyage.name: Tempura
voyage.content: Nice Japanese restaurant, with a very lovely guest woman.

voyage.name: De Pizzabakkers
voyage.content: Hip pizza restaurant, with good stone-baked pizzas. Suitable for children. Almost always busy, so reservation is recommended.

voyage.name: Aguada
voyage.content: Indian and Indonesian influenced. Cosy restaurant. The rendang is a little too sweet but the thali is excellent.

voyage.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
voyage.content: Its label with an ostrich egg is a visual pun, as IJ and 'ei' - the word for egg - sound the same in Dutch. East of the centre, close to Artis Zoo, in a former bath house beside a windmill. A small-scale brewery where delicious beer in several varieties and strengths is brewed and sold - at a bar - on the premises. The beer is available at some specialist beer shops, and is of high quality and, in some cases, alcohol

voyage.name: Café Smit & Voogt
voyage.content: Locals love this place. It is situated inside a beautiful building and has timber booths and seating inside . There is also seating on the footpath which is well placed to catch the afternoon sun. Serves a selection of beers and other alcoholic drinks and also serves food. You can usually get a seat for a drink but better to come early or book for food. Very friendly service.

voyage.name: Eden Lancaster Hotel
voyage.content: A quaint 3-star hotel with 91 rooms and bags of character. Friendly and helpful English-speaking staff, quiet area and very good value for money.

voyage.name: InterContinental Amstel Hotel
voyage.content: Historic 5-star hotel on the banks of Amstel River, near financial, shopping and theater districts. Voted the Netherlands' best in 2008 by Condé Nast Traveller. 19th-century palace, 79 guestrooms and suites, indoor swimming pool, spa facilities including a Turkish bath.

voyage.name: Hotel Allure
voyage.content: Hotel Allure has rooms at Sarphiastraat and also self contained apartments at Plantage Muidergracht. The apartments are a little more expensive on a per person per night basis than the hotel and not quite as clean and tidy but may suit as they have a small kitchen (no washing machine though).

voyage.name: Royal Coster
voyage.content: This stately building is one of Amsterdam's two diamond factories. Guided tours are given showcasing the complicated diamond production process. It looks like just an ordinary jewellery shop, and of course it is, but there is a lot more to it. If you want to purchase diamonds, ask for the tax refund form so you can get up to 12% of the asking price back at the airport.

voyage.name: Diamant Museum
voyage.content: This exhibition is about the history of the diamond trade in Amsterdam.

voyage.name: Heineken Experience
voyage.hours: Sun–Wed 10:30-19:30, last entry 17:15, Thu Fri 10:30-21:00, last entry 18:45
voyage.content: Do not expect a beer museum, but rather to be flooded with Heineken advertisements.

voyage.name: Rijksmuseum
voyage.price: 25 EUR adults, 12.50 EUR European Youth Card, children free, no student discounts
voyage.content: The largest and most prestigious museum for art and history in the Netherlands: works by Vermeer, Rembrandt, and other Dutch masters. Its garden has a curious collection of architecture and has free entrance during museum opening times. Recommend getting there early to avoid long queues and crowds, then head first for the second floor to see the Rembrandt classics and others such as Avercamp's Winter Landscape with S

voyage.name: Stedelijk Museum
voyage.content: The Stedelijk Museum is the municipal museum of modern art. It has a long history, as it first opened in 1874 and has been at its current location since 1895. It was reopened in 2012 after a renovation that took four years: the new building is now locally referred to as the "bath tub" due to its unique shape. The "bath tub" will host newly acquired film and video expositions, while the highlights remain in the old pa

voyage.name: Van Gogh Museum
voyage.price: Adults 25 EUR, students 15 EUR, under 18 free
voyage.content: This museum is dedicated to Vincent van Gogh, a late 19th-century Post-Impressionist Dutch painter. Tickets are available online only, and can be booked out weeks in advance during busy periods. In the museum are many, but not all, of Van Gogh's works. The museum contains some famous paintings like Sunflowers and Potato Eaters, but lacks others such as Starry Night. Also, there are selected works of Monet exhibited t

voyage.name: Moco Museum
voyage.price: Adult €19.50, Youth (13-17) and student €16.50, children (0-12) free
voyage.content: Moco is a private museum of modern and contemporary art.

voyage.name: Museumplein
voyage.content: Not exactly a park, but a large grassed open space. Around its edges are the Rijksmuseum, the Van Gogh Museum, the Stedelijk Museum and the Concertgebouw. On a sunny summer day, many locals chill on the grass lawn on top of the Albert Heijn supermarket.

voyage.name: Sarphatipark
voyage.content: Situated in De Pijp, this is a place where people sunbathe and have picnics in the summer.

voyage.name: Vondelpark
voyage.content: The only large park that is close to the Binnenstad, and definitely the most popular one. Especially in the summer, it is lively and crowded, many locals sit on the grass and enjoy a cold beer or wine. It's a lovely place to just hang out, sit in the sun and meet the locals. Open-air theaters are running in the summer on Friday evenings, Saturdays and Sundays.

voyage.name: Huis met de Kabouters
voyage.content: Named after two gnomes decorating its facade, this building is in a mix of Gothic and Renaissance Revival and includes gargoyles and narrow lancet windows. Built in 1884, it became a rijksmonument in 1984.

voyage.name: Strandzuid
voyage.content: With bar and restaurant

voyage.name: Frans Hals
voyage.content: Those interested in urban renewal may wish to visit Frans Hals, a 19th-century, residential area along the narrow Frans Halsstraat (straat means street). By 2019, the city had removed on-street parking and replaced it with greenery, benches, picnic tables and some playground equipment. There are several restaurants along the street.

voyage.name: Lady Solid
voyage.content: Lady Solid is a life-size statue of a woman in a striking pose standing with arms and feet spread. The statue has a water feature making the artwork controversial as it appears the lady has an incontinence problem. The pumping station features the artwork perhaps as it was "promoting the importance of well-functioning waterways", as suggested by a website on public art. The statue/fountain can be seen from the public

voyage.name: Lomanstraat
voyage.content: A charming photogenic street known for its curiously crooked trees, that form a kind of a tunnel.

voyage.name: Electrische Museumtramlijn Amsterdam
voyage.price: Adult fares vary from €3.50 to €12.50 with reduced rates for seniors (65+) and children (4-11)
voyage.hours: Sundays, April-November, plus Easter & Pentecost Mon, 11:00-17:00
voyage.content: On operating days, the museum runs various vintage trams on two routes. Line 30 runs every 30 minutes along on a 7-km museum rail line to Amstelveen with stops along the route. Station Amstelveen is perhaps the most interesting stop as it is near an attractive small-town area with restaurants. Line 20 runs two trips only around Amsterdam. If you buy a day pass, you can travel both routes.

voyage.name: Concertgebouw
voyage.content: Famous for its orchestra and its acoustics (among the top ten in the world), this is one of the world's most frequently visited concert halls. Classical music is the main fare, but they also bring other kinds of music on stage. They have a free "lunch concert" on Wednesday from 12:30 till 13:00. In the same building is the "Kleine Zaal" ("Small Hall") for more intimate performances, often top-notch as well. It's wort

voyage.name: Friday Night Skate
voyage.content: Put on your skates, and join the popular weekly skate tour (since 1997), a different route every week. Starts every Friday at 20:30 from the Vondelpark (near the former Filmmuseum).

voyage.name: Rialto
voyage.content: For all art-house cinema lovers. All films are shown in their original language with Dutch subtitles. They have late-night and classic showings too. Just a short walk from the Albert Cuyp Market/Heineken Brouwerij, in the nice non-touristy neighborhood De Pijp.

voyage.name: ICE* Amsterdam
voyage.content: During winter time there is an amazing ice rink in Amsterdam at the Museumplein. The open-air ice skating rink that covers 1400 m2 can be found at its usual spot in the heart of Amsterdam and is open daily for all visitors.

voyage.name: Albert Cuyp Market
voyage.content: Largest street market in Amsterdam, and the best-known street market in the country. It is iconic for the "De Pijp" neighborhood and its working-class inhabitants. There is something for everyone here, whether you're looking for delicious Dutch treats, clothing or second-hand cameras. There's also a wide array of stores that cater to the city's Surinamese, Antillean, Turkish and Moroccan inhabitants, giving the marke

voyage.name: Pieter Cornelisz Hooftstraat
voyage.content: Probably the wealthiest street in the country where Dutch celebrities go for a new pair of designer shoes. Better bring a filled wallet if you're planning to buy something here.

voyage.name: Albina
voyage.content: It's cheap and very good. If you arrive around dinnertime you probably have to wait for a table. The surroundings are depressing but the food is so good you will come back anyway.

voyage.name: Tjin's Gelderlandplein
voyage.content: Tasty, great value Surinamese take-out. Sandwiches. Located a short walk from the Zuidas area hotels. A few tables are also available to eat in.

voyage.name: CTaste
voyage.content: Dining in the dark. All waiters are blind, and serve you dinner in a completely dark restaurant. A very weird, but actually quite fun experience.

voyage.name: OCCII
voyage.content: A rock venue for cutting-edge music (punk, noise, riot grrrl, etc.)

voyage.name: Club Media
voyage.content: Completely organic menu, fair selection, good prices, lovely staff, free fruit!

voyage.name: Katsu
voyage.content: Just around the corner from Media, good prices + nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: 't Blauwe Theehuis
voyage.content: Basic bar and beer garden

voyage.name: De Roos
voyage.content: Quite tea house with a small garden.

voyage.name: Flying Pig Uptown
voyage.content: A bit loud and boisterous for travellers looking to relax, but good for those looking to meet people from all over the world and get the true "Amsterdam Experience". Lockers require lockpads, which are not available for rent, only buy for €5.

voyage.name: Hostel Cosmos
voyage.content: Friendly youth hostel.

voyage.name: Sphinx Hotel
voyage.content: From single rooms to five people sharing, steep stairs and no lift, shared or private bathrooms (quite small), very close to the museums.

voyage.name: Van Ostade Bicycle Hotel
voyage.content: Surrounded by fantastic architecture with reasonable rates, even at peak. Rooms from single to quadruple and optional en suite. Comes with free coffee, breakfast and wireless internet access.

voyage.name: ibis Styles Amsterdam City
voyage.content: 3-star hotel. All the floors are reachable by elevator. All rooms have their own private bathrooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Flipper
voyage.content: Attractive, in a peaceful location in a quiet residential area.

voyage.name: Hotel City Garden
voyage.content: The hotel has 70 rooms with stylish interiors and a beautiful view.

voyage.name: citizenM (Amsterdam City)
voyage.content: Second property by citizenM hotels, opened in 2009. Rooms include free WiFi and movies, a rainshower, and an XL kingsize bed with luxury linens.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Amsterdam
voyage.content: Ticks all the main boxes for facilities but about due for a refurbishment.

voyage.name: Park Plaza
voyage.content: Free Wi-Fi in public areas.

voyage.name: Bilderberg Garden Hotel
voyage.content: Five-star hotel just off the Apollolaan.

voyage.name: Hilton Amsterdam
voyage.content: Internationally famous as the site of John Lennon's and Yoko Ono's bed-in. Nationally famous for being where Dutch artist Herman Brood killed himself.

voyage.name: Hotel Okura
voyage.content: Five-star Japanese-owned and -operated hotel with an excellent range of Japanese food, clothing, and book shops in the basement, and wireless internet in the lobby, bar, and conference rooms. The only drawback is that it's relatively distant from the central station (15 minutes by tram), but worth considering if work is paying and you don't mind taking cabs.

voyage.name: Park Hotel Amsterdam
voyage.content: Bang in the middle of Amsterdam between Leidseplein, Rijksmuseum and P.C. Hooftstraat. Four-star hotel spread over several historical buildings. Parking. Very friendly staff.

voyage.name: Conservatorium Hotel
voyage.content: Five-star hotel offers 129 guest suites spread throughout 8 floors.

voyage.name: Hotel JL No76
voyage.content: Hotel JL No76 is a luxury boutique hotel 2½ blocks from Vondelpark.

voyage.name: Museum Het Schip
voyage.content: A museum about the Amsterdam School architectural style, housed in a building that is probably the city's best example of that style entrance.

voyage.name: Rembrandtpark
voyage.content: Not too far west of the Vondelpark, but much quieter and larger in size.

voyage.name: Westerpark
voyage.content: A park at the western edge of the centre, with cultural activities in a former gas factory (Westergasfabriek). Access from Haarlemmerweg.

voyage.name: De 1100 Roe (1674)
voyage.content: In the Ookmeer sports fields along Ma Braunpad.

voyage.name: De 1200 Roe (1632)
voyage.content: Near Seineweg.

voyage.name: De Bloem (1878)
voyage.content: at Nieuwpoortkade.

voyage.name: De Otter (1631)
voyage.content: A restored and functioning sawmill, opposite Buyskade, west of the Jordaan.

voyage.name: Molen van Sloten
voyage.content: In Zuid, the only one open for visitors

voyage.name: Ten Katemarkt
voyage.content: Third largest in Amsterdam with food, households, flowers and clothing.

voyage.name: Dosa
voyage.content: They specialise in traditional Southern Indian cuisine, especially the eponymous 'Dosa' (a rice and lentil pancake with a variety of fillings). The food is outstanding and well worth hunting out. The dosas are exceptional and a treat worthy of a visit by themselves.

voyage.name: Foodhallen
voyage.content: International food court with 20 food-stands housed in a large building that was once a tram depot.

voyage.name: Hap Hmm
voyage.content: Traditional Dutch cuisine. The restaurant may be cramped, but it does serve some quality and rustic Dutch fare. This place is cash only.

voyage.name: Sora Sapporo Ramen - West
voyage.content: Small ramen restaurant with friendly staff, quick service, and good selection of ramen & appetizers. Also serve beer & sake. Closes early and small seating so might want to reserve on weekends.

voyage.name: TonTon Club West
voyage.content: TonTon Club is an excellent place for a good night out. The place has a unique atmosphere with Japan as its inspiration. Upstairs there are arcades and button bashers, downstairs there's room for drinks and board games. You can also order Japanese snacks. Be early as tables are often reserved.

voyage.name: Cafe L'Affice
voyage.content: Small bar with friendly staff and a cosy and candle-lit atmosphere. Selection of beers on tap and in bottles, including a triple blonde specially made for the bar. Small selection of bar food as well.

voyage.name: Club 8
voyage.content: A large alternative place with lots of art on its walls. There's ping pong, a very local and fairly young crowd.

voyage.name: Hotel ABBA
voyage.content: Cheap but clean hotel, close to the Van Gogh and Rijksmuseum.

voyage.name: MissOrtelia
voyage.content: Free bikes - Wi-fi free - breakfast included.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express Amsterdam - Sloterdijk Station
voyage.content: This HIExpress is right in the midst of the web of tracks extending around Sloterdijk station, making it very convenient for travel to just about any point in Amsterdam. That said, the actual area around the hotel is a sombre office park and a huge "transferium", so it is best to only come there to sleep and have (free) breakfast.

voyage.name: Meininger Hotel Amsterdam City West
voyage.content: The Meininger chain's properties sit somewhere between budget hotels and hostels, with available multi-person rooms with bunk beds and on-site laundrette. The hotel is relatively new and visually attractive if rather basic inside. Again, staying in the midst of Sloterdijk is great for transit possibilities and rather unexciting regarding everything else.

voyage.name: Stayokay Vondelpark
voyage.content: Fairly large youth hostel, very clean and professional, operated by the Dutch affiliate of Hostelling International. Next to the pleasant Vondelpark, puts you on the south-western side of the city center and just a few blocks from the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum. The breakfast is filling and has a social atmosphere. This location is popular with school groups. Bring a padlock for your locker, or purchase one

voyage.name: Ramada Apollo Amsterdam Centre
voyage.content: The Ramada is a solid property, but calling it "Amsterdam Centre" was not even close to reality, as the hotel is at the remote end of Rembrandtpark, close to the A10 ring road running across Amsterdam-West. That said, you will find getting to the city quite easy thanks to them tram 13 stop at the hotel's back and the park provides a tranquil environment. The best rooms have great views of Amsterdam over the park; the

voyage.name: Roemer Hotel
voyage.content: Trendy boutique hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Espresso City Center
voyage.content: Near Leidseplein with tram connections and bus to airport. Near Vondelpark and Museumplein. Buffet breakfast available at extra cost. Unlimited free coffee (including koffie verkeerd, the Dutch equivalent of café au lait) for guests in the lobby area.

voyage.name: Amsterdam Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: At the border of Oud-West and the Canal District, this old-fashioned Marriott can offer a relatively attractive rate and still has a convenient location for exploring the city centre.

voyage.name: Park Plaza Amsterdam Airport
voyage.content: The hotel has 19 meeting rooms as well as 6 business suites. The hotel provides free shuttle service from and to the airport as well as free wi-fi in public areas.

voyage.name: D'Admiraal (1792)
voyage.content: Windmill on the bank of the Noordhollands Kanaal in the north, ferry from Central Station.

voyage.name: STRAAT Museum
voyage.price: Adults 19.50 EUR, 13-18 yrs 9.50 EUR, 0-12 yrs free
voyage.content: Museum depicting street art in a large indoor exhibition.

voyage.name: EYE Film Institute Netherlands
voyage.content: EYE is an institute dedicated to the preservation of film for future generations. It is the successor of the Filmmuseum. It has four film theatres with alternative screenings such as art films. In April the Imagine Film Festival is held here with screenings dedicated to exploitation, cult and lower-budget films. Well worth it if you're a fan of the genre.

voyage.name: Café Modern B.V.
voyage.content: A restaurant and cafe in a hall which used to be a bank.

voyage.name: Café-restaurant Stork
voyage.content: A fish and seafood restaurant in an old factory on the banks of the river.

voyage.name: Hangar Amsterdam
voyage.content: A redesigned aircraft hangar, turned restaurant.

voyage.name: Mount Everest Tandoori
voyage.content: An Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Vegetarian friendly.

voyage.name: Pllek
voyage.content: A bar and restaurant in an old industrial area, by the river.

voyage.name: Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Noord
voyage.content: 3-star hotel with 86 rooms.

voyage.name: Amstelstation murals
voyage.content: In the hall of Amstel railway station, there are several murals created in 1939 by Dutch artist Peter Alma, including a large mural at each end of the hall with a train motif.

voyage.name: Floating houses
voyage.content: There are two clusters of floating houses over a body of water. These small, modern houses are linked by a grid of walkways lined with railings holding life preservers and bicycles.

voyage.name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam
voyage.content: Ethnographic and cultural museum about Africa, Asia and South America. Includes an excellent cafe which sells food from around the world. Tickets are discounted if reserved online.

voyage.name: Oosterpark
voyage.content: Close to Plantage, this park holds several multicultural festivals throughout the year.

voyage.name: Diemerpark
voyage.content: This is a large park, a little like a dune park.

voyage.name: Flevopark
voyage.content: The Flevopark is in the Indische Buurt, at the eastern end of the Insulindeweg, next to the Jewish cemetery, the Flevoparkbad swimming pool, and the Nieuwe Diep inlet. There are two cafés open in spring/summer/autumn time and one festival each year.

voyage.name: Frankendael
voyage.content: Frankendael is a house built in 1733 in Watergraafsmeer. The house is surrounded by a pleasant park. Take tram 9, get off at the stop "Hugo de Vrieslaan".

voyage.name: Bimhuis
voyage.content: World-class jazz and improvised music venue, five minutes by foot from Centraal Station.

voyage.name: Muziekgebouw aan't IJ
voyage.content: Modern music concerts and classical music with a twist. A free concert is given every second Tuesday of the month at 12:30.

voyage.name: Dappermarkt
voyage.content: In the east, behind the zoo, and was voted best market in the Netherlands.

voyage.name: Bij'tij
voyage.content: Boutique.

voyage.name: Bliksem en Sterren
voyage.content: For kids's clothing.

voyage.name: Design020
voyage.content: A large interior design centre that is an architectural highlight by itself. Plenty of interesting interior shops like Kartell and Kasstoor, and also don't miss the café as it has a roof terrace with a great view on the water. Free parking.

voyage.name: Flo 4 Kidz
voyage.content: For kids' clothing.

voyage.name: Frontrow
voyage.content: Boutique.

voyage.name: Ien Lifestyleshop
voyage.content: Boutique.

voyage.name: Sevenlands
voyage.content: Boutique.

voyage.name: SUBURB Denim
voyage.content: Boutique.

voyage.name: Tjikky+Ko
voyage.content: For kids's clothing.

voyage.name: Boerenjongens Eetwinkel
voyage.content: A deli shop annex lunch room with products from the region.

voyage.name: IJsburg
voyage.content: Ice cream shop.

voyage.name: Biertuin
voyage.content: Oktoberfest-style biergarten, so expect long tables and a wide variety of bottled beers available. It has a nice atmosphere during warm summer evenings. Try the Hamburger Deluxe or chicken menus. And come early, as it is often crowded. Reservations cannot be made, but you can wait outside with a beer until seating is available.

voyage.name: Bloem op IJburg
voyage.content: Italian restaurant.

voyage.name: Silk Road Restaurant
voyage.content: Eastern and Western fusion meals with both à la carte and (on highly occupied days o­nly) a live cooking theme buffet. The restaurant has a view of the river IJ. Open 7 days per week for lunch and dinner.

voyage.name: Espressofabriek
voyage.content: Coffee bar.

voyage.name: N.A.P.
voyage.content: A harbour-side cafe and restaurant with a view of the marina. You can just stop by for a cup of coffee, have breakfast, lunch or dinner. Stylish interior.

voyage.name: Delirium Café Amsterdam
voyage.content: With over 500 bottled beers and 20 craft beers on draft, the biggest craft beer bar in Amsterdam.

voyage.name: Panama
voyage.content: This nightclub is relatively close to the city centre. It has its fair share of nice nights and the view on the water is excellent.

voyage.name: Canvas
voyage.content: A restaurant-bar-club, this urban and edgy den in a former newspaper office is a great place to go out at night. With nice views of the city and a varied music repertoire (alternative, jazz, funk), it's one of the hidden secrets too often overlooked by foreign visitors. Try one of the cocktails.

voyage.name: Camping Zeeburg
voyage.content: This campground is near the city. It has camping cabins, wagonettes, tent sites and RV sites. A good store, free wifi and restaurant/bar round out the amenities. A good, clean and cheap place to stay if you do not mind walking to the bathroom and paying €.80 for a hot shower.

voyage.name: Stayokay Zeeburg
voyage.content: This 480-bed hostel is located to the east of the city centre in a typical Amsterdam neighbourhood. Amsterdam's historic centre is less than 15 minutes away by bike or tram. The hostel is in the same building as Studio K, a budget diner and movie theatre. Children under 12 must stay in private rooms and everyone under 18 must be accompanied by an adult.

voyage.name: Generator Hostel Amsterdam
voyage.content: This former university building can host up to 564 guests in twin and quadruple rooms. It has spacious social areas with creative design touches all over the building. The old lecture rooms and hall have been turned into bars and a relaxation room. This place is excellent value for groups and budget travellers, with quadruple rooms for €60 or single (bunk) beds in shared rooms for €15. Bathrooms are en-suite. If you'

voyage.name: Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Amstel
voyage.content: 3 star-hotel with 192 rooms. Due to its central location, the Amsterdam RAI, Amsterdam ArenA and Ziggo Dome are very well accessible from Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Amstel. Public transport is located within a 10-minute walk.

voyage.name: Mövenpick Hotel
voyage.content: The hotel is in the Eastern Docklands, the renewed area of the city centre.

en.title: Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
